trial_court: learned J.M.F.C., Hinjilicut (G.R. Case No.3 of 2013)
case_name: Kora Prasad Padhi And Others vs State Of Odisha

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Kora Prasad Padhi and others (husband, wife, etc.)

facts_of_case: Petitioners' wife lodged an F.I.R. leading to criminal proceeding; parties settled and filed joint application for mutual divorce under Hindu Marriage Act, 1955; court allowed application and dissolved marriage.

legal_principles.principle: A criminal proceeding can be quashed even if the offences are not compoundable, in order to advance the cause of justice.
legal_principles.held: The settled position of law is that even if offences alleged in a criminal proceeding not to be compoundable, it can still be quashed keeping in view the larger interest of the parties.

legal_principles.principle: The court can exercise powers under Article 226 of the Constitution and Section 482 Cr.P.C. to quash a criminal proceeding.
legal_principles.held: This Court has held and observed that there is no bar in exercising powers under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and also Section 482 Cr.P.C. in order to quash a criminal proceeding, even when the offences are not compoundable or it is required to advance the cause of justice.

outcome.final_order: Criminal proceeding in G.R. Case No.3 of 2013 quashed.
